title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 concurrency ladder: vLLM one-shot baseline
subtitle: vLLM 0.27.1 + MTP, C=1..16 (throughput) and C=1..128 (energy leg), on the published ladder instrument; no Metrale Engine leg at this instrument yet
aggregate: mean tok/s over 3 timed reps (1 warmup discarded)
subject_note: No series has role "subject": no Metrale Engine run exists at this instrument for this checkpoint. This manifest deliberately mirrors bench/ladder38/published.json so that when one does, it is added as a series with role "subject" whose sources name its raw harness files, and gen-ladder.mjs scores the pair with the same code it scores the dense ladder with. Until then the generator emits no rows and no summary for this ladder, and the site says so instead of drawing a zero.

workload.checkpoint_note: MoE 35B, 256 experts top-8 (~3B active per token), FP8 block-scale weights, 40 layers; architecture qwen3_5_moe
workload.isl_note: ~200 rendered prompt tokens after the chat template (prompt_tokens_per_req is 200 in every rep of the raw file)
workload.sampling_parity: presence_penalty and frequency_penalty pinned to 0.0 by the harness

box.name: dgx2 (spark-43fa)
box.gpu: NVIDIA GB10 Grace Blackwell, 121.7 GB unified
box.note: the box the published dense ladder's vLLM legs ran on; the serve was refused unless nothing else held the box

harness_shas.41e242c072: vLLM MoE leg, the only leg in this manifest. This was the sha256 of the copy committed at bench/ladder38/harness_w55_conc_ladder.py (md5 4aa694d8aabe404edc8f1e3eb2acbf31) when it ran; that file's comments have been edited since, so gen-ladder.mjs's harness_repo_sha256 (the tree copy) no longer equals it. The dense ladder's raw files carry earlier revisions of this same file (6412b12d4d, 1c77e1d8e9, 1f10d4887b); the deck prints the recorded and the repo hash side by side.
harness_shas.55a5963e4b: The ENERGY leg (vllm-mtp-energy), 2026-09-28. harness_w56_conc_ladder.py -- the w55 harness plus power_window.py, which records gpu_rail_energy_j per rep; w55 has no power sampling, which is why vllm-mtp carries no joules. This is the sha256 of the copy committed at bench/ladder38/harness_w56_conc_ladder.py at 7cd54d45 and the one copied to dgx2 for the run: the raw file's driver_sha256 equals it (the harness hashes itself at startup). The dense ladder's energy leg ran an earlier revision of the same file (664302439b); the two differ in comments and in the new detection of in-band SSE error frames and truncated streams (both turn a would-be silent success into a counted error), not in the request body; power_window.py, which does the integral, differs only in comments.
harness_shas.equivalence: One revision, one leg. The copy on dgx2 (/home/claude/ladder38-pinned/) was a DIFFERENT, older revision and was replaced with the repo copy before measuring; the driver_sha256 in the raw file is the proof of which copy ran, and the generator refuses any raw file whose driver sha is not listed here.

series.label: vLLM + MTP
series.parity_note: Matched to the Metrale Engine MoE ladder recipe adjudicated by the bench-parity oracle on 2026-09-19 before the run: ctx 2048, batch cap 128, util 0.85, bf16 KV, MTP K=4, thinking off, presence/frequency penalties 0.0, and Metrale Engine pinned to fifo scheduling (its MoE recipe defaults to slai, which vLLM has no counterpart for). That is the configuration a Metrale Engine leg at this instrument must serve to be scored against this series; no such leg exists yet.
series.build_note: Read from `docker image inspect vllm/vllm-openai:latest` on dgx2 on 2026-09-19, not remembered: image id sha256:2c211a1273b48e8929f893b267aeb1509e6b84654cdbde1bad56d79e3964224d, label ai.vllm.image.tag=vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1, vLLM commit 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac, created 2026-08-11. It is the same digest the dense ladder's vLLM legs ran, and a container from it logs `version 0.27.1` at startup.

kernel_override.what: vLLM is NOT running its own default FP8 MoE kernel on this hardware. Its default FP8 block-scale MoE path selects DeepGEMM; these two variables force the Marlin FP8 path instead.
kernel_override.why: DeepGEMM crashes at WEIGHT LOAD on GB10 (SM121), before any inference: the first attempt of the evening died at 79% of the load. The same SM120/SM121 incompatibility already recorded for the TRTLLM, CuteDSL, DeepGEMM and Triton MoE backends; only CUTLASS and Marlin work on this box.
kernel_override.error: deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block -> transform_sf_into_required_layout: RuntimeError: Assertion error (deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60): Unknown SF transformation
kernel_override.scope: A kernel selection, not a workload axis: it moves nothing the parity oracle adjudicates, but a reader comparing engines deserves to know.

series.cli: docker run --network host --gpus all --ipc=host -v /home/claude/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 -e VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1 vllm/vllm-openai:latest --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype auto --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
series.speculation: vLLM's own MTP drafter, K=4 (--speculative-config method=mtp, num_speculative_tokens=3)
series.instrument_note: kv_cache_dtype is bf16 although the command says `--kv-cache-dtype auto`: auto takes the model dtype, and `--dtype bfloat16` is set, so the KV cache is bf16 BECAUSE the dtype is bfloat16. Spelled `bf16` because that is how a Metrale Engine gate record writes serve_overrides.kv_cache_dtype, which is what this fingerprint is compared against; vLLM's own spelling is bfloat16. No prompt_mode: the ladder harness has no fixture, it sends a nonce-prefixed padded prompt, so a gate record (natural fixture) can never fingerprint as this instrument. prompt_mode is essay because the pinned harness defaults to it (bench/ladder38/harness_w55_conc_ladder.py:75, PROMPT_MODE = os.environ.get("W55_PROMPT_MODE", "essay")) and this series' recorded env (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1) does not set it. DERIVED, NOT RECORDED: the raw file carries isl, osl, reps, warmup, temperature, seed and chat_template_kwargs but not prompt_mode, so re-check this if the raw file is ever replaced -- a harness that recorded it would make this a fact instead of an inference. It is declared because ladder-baselines.js treats an undeclared axis as a DIFFERENCE, never a match: without it a future concurrency-sweep-moe gate record measured on this exact instrument could never be drawn against this bar.

unmeasured.reason: The ladder stops at C=16 because of memory, not because of time. GB10 carries 121.7 GB of UNIFIED memory shared between CPU and GPU -- there is no separate VRAM to fall back on. At C >= 32 the vLLM + MTP working set (per-sequence KV cache plus MTP's speculative draft state) outgrows what that shared pool can carry alongside the host, and because the pool is shared, exhausting it takes the whole machine down rather than failing a single allocation: three physical powercycles in one day, at the safe util 0.85 and with --max-num-seqs already capped. We did not isolate it further because every attempt costs the box. These rungs were deliberately not run. They have no value here: not zero, not interpolated, and the generator refuses a raw file that contains them. 2026-09-28: this one-shot was not re-run, but the energy leg (vllm-mtp-energy) did drive C=32/64/128 on the same box with the same command, one fresh container per rung. All three rungs completed, with zero request errors and no stall; host MemAvailable never fell below 4.9 GB, and the box stayed up. So the memory explanation above held on 2026-08-18, and was not reproduced on 2026-09-28.

series.source_note: One-shot: measured once, on 2026-09-19 on dgx2, and never re-run. Every rung comes from the single raw file vllm_moe_c1_16.json (sha256 7788d19a16bb32466a53f72fc13c70c8f9352fb888b758f786a54c1a6b7ad648, byte-identical to dgx2:/home/claude/ladder-moe-baseline/). Two earlier attempts the same evening produced no numbers and are not here: one died in DeepGEMM at weight load (kernel_override), one ran the ladder against a serve whose harness preflight had failed (no first token; TypeError on ttft_p50_ms). Zero request errors at every rung.

series.instrument_note: Measured 2026-09-28 on spark-43fa (dgx2) to give the Cost tab a MoE vLLM leg that carries JOULES; vllm-mtp is throughput-only. Same engine (vLLM 0.27.1), same image, same checkpoint, same command and same instrument as vllm-mtp. Throughput landed within 1.6% of it on every rung (52.92/92.10/145.65/222.64/329.97 vs 52.11/93.16/145.94/222.08/329.93 tok/s; +1.6/-1.1/-0.2/+0.3/+0.0%), on the same box on a different day, which is the agreement that makes the energy quotable. Energy is GPU RAIL ONLY: nvidia-smi power.draw.average at 250 ms, integrated over each rep's own window -- the same source and cadence the Metrale Engine gate sampler integrates -- so Grace and LPDDR5X are outside it for both engines. An NVML cumulative-energy-counter sidecar ran beside it as a cross-check and read 1.2-3.7% lower per rung (higher gap at higher load), the known bias of integrating power.draw.average; ratios between two engines measured the same way hold. kv_cache_dtype is bf16 although the command says `--kv-cache-dtype auto`: auto takes the model dtype and `--dtype bfloat16` is set; spelled `bf16` because that is how a Metrale Engine gate record writes serve_overrides.kv_cache_dtype. prompt_mode essay: the pinned harness defaults to it (PROMPT_MODE = os.environ.get("W55_PROMPT_MODE", "essay")) and neither the run's environment nor the box's shell profile sets W55_PROMPT_MODE. parity is `matched` because every instrument axis equals vllm-mtp's; this manifest has no subject series, so no published ratio is computed against either leg.

Every rung comes from the single raw file vllm_moe_energy_c1_16.json (sha256 eb4f73b0c9ca76d8c6a6e0982050897c94a501417f04c5a8718bba64353d2eb4). Zero request errors, every rep gpu_rail_trustworthy with 98-100% sample coverage, no HW power brake; GPU die 58-77 C across the ladder.
series.wide_note: C=32/64/128 measured 2026-09-28 on spark-43fa (dgx2) with nothing else on the box, after the owner lifted the pause on vLLM at C >= 32. Each rung ran on its own FRESH container, because vLLM+MTP has taken a GB10 down at these widths before: C=32 20:14-20:19, C=64 20:30-20:38, C=128 20:49-21:02 UTC. The command is the one above, verbatim, started detached and named (`docker run -d --name vllm-wide-moe-c<C>`). The image was checked before each launch: id 2c211a1273b4, repo digest 0a51ea5b4ae2, label v0.27.1. A stall probe beside the harness watched vLLM's /metrics and host memory. It never fired; the lowest host MemAvailable was 4.9 GB, at C=128. vLLM sized its KV cache at 327,680-331,655 tokens, 160x the 2048-token context, so all 128 streams ran at once (/metrics read 128 running). Zero request errors. Every rep is gpu_rail_trustworthy with 99.5-99.9% sample coverage and no HW power brake; the GPU die peaked at 77-83 C. Raw files: vllm_moe_energy_c32.json (sha256 dde20fd70a06f122393e1ece85de4f7061cecb3ccc23db4a81663e75c609e898), vllm_moe_energy_c64.json (sha256 5c06ac7647a92a9f3cb2261f701e0659f86413332b629975a97ef9fd0139ca66), vllm_moe_energy_c128.json (sha256 a9dd852f81452de53c41b6dfa6b40c9ac17190f2c0f4d81abbe4aab4a5954adc).
